figures.title: The n × n score matrix is the quadratic term
figures.caption: Every query scores every key, so the score matrix is n × n; the causal mask keeps the lower triangle. At n = 130,659, n² = 1.707 × 10^10 entries. Stored as dense fp16 at 2 bytes each, one head in one layer is 34.1 GB, roughly 30.6% of the engine's 111.5 GB, and the product over heads and layers passes the budget many times over. The grid is a schematic 10 × 10; the numbers are the chapter's.
figures.alt: A 10 by 10 causal score grid. Filled cells are allowed query-key pairs with j ≤ i; the upper triangle is masked. Row 8 is highlighted. The note gives n = 130,659, n² = 1.707 × 10^10 entries, and 34.1 GB per head per layer in fp16.

data.note: Schematic 10 × 10 causal grid, not to scale. At n = 130,659 the matrix has n² = 1.707 × 10^10 entries; the causal triangle has n(n+1)/2. In fp16 at 2 bytes per entry, one head in one layer is 34.1 GB, about 30.6% of the engine's 111.5 GB; all heads and layers pass the budget many times over.

figures.title: Quadratic and linear attention on log-log axes
figures.caption: On log-log axes, quadratic attention rises with slope 2 and linear attention with slope 1. The plotted points run from n = 128 to n = 2048 and are relative costs computed from n/128, an illustrative normalization; the chapter's absolute counts at n = 130,659 are in the note. At n = 4096 the quadratic cost is 1024× the n = 128 cost and linear is 32×. The crossover at n = d = 128 is where linear attention becomes cheaper.
figures.alt: A log-log plot. The horizontal axis is sequence length n from 1 to 10,000; the vertical axis is cost relative to n = 128 from 1 to 1,000. The quadratic line passes through (128, 1), (256, 4), (512, 16), (1024, 64) and (2048, 256); the linear line passes through (128, 1), (256, 2), (512, 4), (1024, 8) and (2048, 16). The quadratic line is twice as steep.

data.note: Relative cost is illustrative: quadratic attention scales as (n/128)², linear attention as n/128; the crossover is at n = d = 128, which the chapter states. At n = 4096 the quadratic ratio is 1024 and the linear ratio is 32. Absolute figures at n = 130,659: 1.707 × 10^10 score entries; 2.185 × 10^12 multiply-adds for the scores per head per layer, and the same again for value aggregation, so 4.37 × 10^12; a 4,096-token window cuts entries to 5.35 × 10^8, 32× fewer; linear attention costs 2.14 × 10^9 operations.
